scenes.headline: Asset Bundles & CI/CD
scenes.subtitle: Package and deploy Databricks projects as code
scenes.narration: Databricks Asset Bundles define jobs, pipelines, and resources as code for reproducible, automated deployment.

scenes.headline: What a bundle contains
items: Jobs, pipelines, and cluster definitions as YAML
Per-environment targets like dev, staging, prod
scenes.narration: A bundle captures your workflows and resources in version-controlled YAML. It references the notebooks and code they run. Targets let one definition deploy consistently across dev, staging, and production.

scenes.headline: A databricks.yml bundle
scenes.code:
bundle:
  name: sales_pipeline

targets:
  dev:
    default: true
    workspace:
      host: https://dev.cloud.databricks.com
  prod:
    workspace:
      host: https://prod.cloud.databricks.com

resources:
  jobs:
    daily_etl:
      name: daily_etl
      tasks:
        - task_key: run_dlt
          pipeline_task:
            pipeline_id: ${resources.pipelines.etl.id}
scenes.narration: This bundle declares a job named daily_etl that triggers a DLT pipeline. Two targets point at separate dev and prod workspaces from the same definition. Deploying is then as simple as running databricks bundle deploy against a chosen target.

scenes.headline: CI/CD flow
scenes.narration: A commit triggers your CI pipeline to validate and test the bundle. The bundle is deployed to staging for integration checks. Once verified, the same artifact is promoted to production.

scenes.headline: Why bundles matter
items: Environment parity from one source of truth
scenes.narration: Defining resources as code makes deployments repeatable and reviewable. A single source of truth keeps environments in parity and avoids drift. Automation eliminates error-prone manual configuration in the UI.

scenes.text: Asset Bundles turn Databricks projects into versioned, deployable code.
scenes.narration: Commit, review, and promote your pipelines just like any other software.
